prompts.tree: Use case: stylized-concept. Production GAME SPRITE, one single mature rural OAK TREE, isolated on true transparent background, full tree including root flare, no ground scenery, no lettering, no separate reference panels. Sophisticated richly painted PIXEL ART for a medieval 2D three-quarter MMORPG, matching finely worked irregular stone-and-timber cottage sprites with wooden shingle roofs. NOT cartoon, not vector, not low-poly, not a smooth 3D render. Crisp deliberate pixel clusters, restrained 100-160-color feel, readable at native gameplay size around 450 pixels tall. Design the FORMS first: broad asymmetrical oak crown built from 5-7 overlapping primary leaf masses, with secondary lobes, deep cool pockets between masses, small meaningful sky openings revealing connected branches; irregular but carefully stepped outer edge. Leaf groups follow each curved mass and occlude each other, never uniform confetti or repeated circles. Upper-left warm sunlight on top/left planes, rich mid green dominant, cool dark forest-green underplanes, sparing yellow-green accents. Robust tapering crooked trunk with a visible branching fork supporting the canopy, cylindrical form with lit left face and shaded right face, longitudinal irregular bark plates, root flare at a very narrow ground anchor. Trunk lower stem narrow relative to crown (approximately 1/20 canopy width) so an actor can pass close to its sides; roots are visual contacts, not an enormous blocking mound. Canopy roughly 65% of tree height, crown wider than lower trunk, slight windward asymmetry. No baked broad ground shadow, just subtle root contact, no floating foliage, no flat oval canopy. Entire subject inside generous transparent margins. Do not draw any house, human, UI or props.
prompts.variant: Use case: precise-object-edit. Use this oak-tree sprite as the art-direction reference and create ONE closely related second OAK TREE FORM VARIATION for the same medieval 2D three-quarter pixel-art game. Keep the refined material language, warm upper-left light, cool forest-green undersides, irregular bark, carefully clustered leaf detail and comparable apparent age and scale. Change the actual branching topology and outline: a narrower taller canopy, two distinct forked main branches, trunk gently leaning LEFT then counterbalancing RIGHT, a small intentional opening between the high left crown mass and the right lower mass. Do not mirror the original. Reduce the bulky lower-right lobe and lift the left branch. Show a coherent tapering trunk connecting every main foliage group, narrow ground stem approximately 1/20 crown width, root flare at bottom. 5-7 overlapping volumetric canopy masses, no repeated circles, no confetti, no smooth 3D gradients or vector outlines. Crisp sophisticated painted pixel clusters compatible with detailed stone/timber cottage game sprites. TRUE transparent background, no ground plane, no broad baked shadow, no text or additional objects. Leave at least 6 percent clear transparent margin on EVERY side, including above the highest leaf and below the roots; whole tree inside frame. This is a distinct sibling tree, not a recolor or scaling of the reference.
prompts.rock: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game SPRITE of ONE substantial weathered fieldstone BOULDER for a detailed medieval pixel-art 2D three-quarter MMORPG. Isolated on real transparent background, full object with transparent margin, no scenery or grass carpet, no typography, no human or house. Think an irregular squat fractured sedimentary boulder, three or four convincing major facets, a broad slanted upper-left top plane lit warm, one dark cool right side, one broken front face. Not a symmetrical gem, not a low-poly 3D rock, not a flat grey texture. The stone has heavy mass, a grounded slightly uneven base, an offset broken shoulder and a smaller attached fractured projection; fine restrained mineral inclusions, a few structural cracks that follow fractures and short discontinuous warm rim edges. Dense detail subordinate to large planes, roughly equivalent craft quality to sophisticated stone-and-timber cottage sprites with finely worked masonry and wood shingles. Original crisp painted pixel art, no blurry gradients, no smooth vector shapes, no heavy black cartoon border, no arbitrary speckle. Stone colours warm grey ochre highlights, grey-beige midplanes, cool grey-olive lower shadow; very small coherent moss colonies confined to low wet creases, not all-green rock. Upper-left illumination, visible top and two side planes, camera looking down about30degrees, orthographic three-quarter view, footprint wider than tall. No broad cast ground shadow, just darkest contact at the immediate bottom. Must read at final gameplay native size about200px wide by140px tall.
prompts.smallStone: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE isolated small broken fieldstone slab, a sibling asset for a sophisticated medieval 2D three-quarter pixel-art RPG, true transparent background with generous clear margins, NO text or scenery. Different silhouette from a round boulder: long low asymmetrical wedge, one raised cracked shoulder on the left, chipped down front-right edge, broad warm sunlit top plane and cool grey-brown front and right planes. Heavy grounded stone with coherent fracture planes, a few structural cracks and tiny moss in basal creases. Match the fine stone-and-timber cottage pixel-art finish: irregular warm grey/ochre stone, cool grey-olive shadow, crisp pixel clusters and fine intentional texture subordinate to form, NOT vector, cartoon, low-poly render, random grey speckle or smooth blur. Upper-left warm light, top plus two sides visible in orthographic 3/4. Final game size about140px wide by75px tall, clear useful planes at that size. No broad baked ground shadow, no grass carpet, no dirt oval, whole object visible.
